title: You Swear You Blocked Background Voices, Yet Your Own Mouth Followed the Ignored Ear
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Anne Treisman (1960/1964): Attenuation Theory — Why Your Ignored Ear Suddenly Hijacks Your Mouth When the Story Jumps Ears!, grounded in Anne Treisman (1964) (Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior). Empirical findings show that by 1959, attention psychology was split by a paradox: Colin Cherry & Donald Broadbent (1958) claimed an early mechanical switch blocks 100% of unattended meaning — yet why do you whip your head around across a noisy party the instant someone whispers YOUR OWN NAME, 'Fire!', or your child's cry?.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how auditory cortex, Wernicke's area, parietal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that at age 24 at Oxford (1960 Quarterly Journal; *1964 JVLVB & British Medical Bulletin, SRC1, SRC2), Anne Treisman designed a delightfully sneaky dichotic shadowing test: Volunteers shadowed the Right Ear strictly ('Repeat ONLY the right ear, ignore the left ear completely!') while hearing coherent prose ('Sitting at a mahogany table with her head in her hands...'*).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Anne Treisman (1964). Monitoring and storage of irrelevant messages in selective attention. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5371(64)80015-3
- Barbara Tversky (2020). Anne Marie Treisman (1937–2018). American Psychologist. https://doi.org/10.1037/amp0000605
- Anne Treisman, Gina Geffen (1967). Selective Attention: Perception or Response? Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1080/14640746708400062
